findings.title: PID snapshot presence is not exact-entry termination evidence
findings.trigger: Controlled first owned-job CloseHandle failure, fallback retained-launcher termination and retry job close; then launcher communicate succeeds and a snapshot contains the entry marker PID.
findings.reason: Windows NativeMemory.inventory returns PID -> (parent PID, None) from Toolhelp without creation identity, retained exact entry handle, signaled state or exit code. OwnedProcess retains its launcher, and communicate waits that Popen process, not a separately identified interpreter entry. The assertion therefore conflates numeric snapshot membership with exact entry execution state.
findings.correction: Replace this liveness oracle with a separately retained, verified exact-entry process observer acquired before fault injection. Keep all existing fallback, owned-handle, controlled-error and job-close assertions; unknown observation must fail, not pass.

supported_facts.fact: Windows inventory enumerates Toolhelp PID and parent values with no creation or exit-state measurement.

Start retains and assigns the Popen launcher; cleanup first attempts job close, calls TerminateProcess on held handles, independently closes them, retries the job close and terminates the original Popen process. There is no retained-entry wait in this path.
The actual entry PID comes from the synthetic marker. Fault assertions are followed by communicate(timeout=5) on the launcher and immediate global numeric snapshot exclusion.

External TerminateProcess initiates asynchronous termination. Microsoft recommends waiting on the process handle to establish completion; pending I/O and open process handles affect completion/object lifetime.
A terminated process object becomes signaled and can remain valid while handles to it are open; launcher termination alone does not establish child termination.
Waiting on a process needs SYNCHRONIZE. Require WAIT_OBJECT_0; timeout, failed or unexpected status denies. Never close the observer while its wait is pending.

Exit query needs query-information rights and a successful return. The controlled fixture must not use exit code STILL_ACTIVE as an application exit value; query code alone is not a substitute for the signaled-handle wait.

independent_failure_report.proposal_assessment: The proposed qualification-only retained-entry observer is supported and more precise than the failed PID inventory oracle. Approval of actual corrective source and execution remains separate; this report approves the design direction only, without modifying runtime or enlarging its timeout.
corrective_source_obligations: Acquire OpenProcess with explicit pointer-width HANDLE prototype and SYNCHRONIZE|PROCESS_QUERY_LIMITED_INFORMATION, noninheritable; reject null/invalid handles. Put every successful acquisition immediately inside guaranteed cleanup ownership.

Before injecting the close fault, verify GetProcessId equals the exact synthetic marker PID, GetProcessTimes creation identity succeeds and IsProcessInJob on the retained observer and original still-owned job succeeds with true membership. Do not reacquire a PID after cleanup and treat a new object as the original.

Keep the observer separate from owner.handles so fallback cleanup cannot close the handle being waited on. Preserve original controlled CloseHandle failure, fallback attempt and second-job-close assertions unchanged.

Start a single five-second settle deadline after owner cleanup, use its remaining budget for launcher communicate and exact-entry WaitForSingleObject. Do not silently create two independent five-second waits. A deadline expiry, unknown state, failed wait or failed exit query fails qualification.

Require WAIT_OBJECT_0 and successful GetExitCodeProcess with controlled-fixture code not STILL_ACTIVE. This witnesses termination of that process object, not destruction of every kernel object or full physical settlement.

Independently close the observer exactly once in finally even when acquisition verification, communicate, wait, exit query or assertions fail. Always attempt existing owned cleanup; preserve the original failure with cleanup failure as cause/note rather than replacing it. A close-only failure must fail.

Protect the entire post-launch marker/observer acquisition sequence, including marker timeout/read/identity failures, under owned launcher/job cleanup. Bind exact source deltas and add meaningful inert wait/identity/membership/deadline/close-priority negatives before any new native execution.

Preserve this original failed main run/log and the prior scoped successes truthfully in the same EQ084 corrective delivery. No unchanged rerun, no old failure promotion to PASS and no Released/Done until corrected current gates qualify.
diagnostic_limits: The log proves the numeric entry PID appeared in the snapshot and the test/build failed. It does not contain exact-entry retained-handle signaled state, exit code or creation identity at the assertion.

Asynchronous exit, PID reuse and retained process-object/snapshot behavior are possible explanations, not established causes. The repeated parent value does not resolve liveness or identity without creation/state evidence.

No executed leak, surviving interpreter, actual runtime defect, attack or whole-kernel resource failure is established by this log alone. The failed qualification still remains a real release-blocking failure.
Prior reviewed SDK/resilience successes and scoped staging replay remain historical evidence, but no complete actual-main gate exists while this foundation failure is unresolved.
